steps.referenceSource: INDEPENDENT ORACLE, NOT AN AURORA-TO-AURORA BASELINE: this frame is rendered by Microsoft Edge, captured on 2026-10-17 with `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" --headless=new --force-device-scale-factor=1 --window-size=1280,638 --hide-scrollbars --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --user-data-dir=<scratch>\edge-prof-geom --screenshot=aurora-browser/tests/reference/flex-geometry.edge.png file:///<repo>/aurora-browser/tests/reference/flex-geometry.html`. The fixture holds five box-geometry cases, each a solid rectangle so that no glyph can decide a pixel, at the engine's own 1280x638 page viewport and 1x device scale: (1) a flex container with padding 0 30px must stretch its item across its 300px content box, not its content box minus its own padding; (2) a flex row with align-items:center must paint the item's whole box centred, so the rectangle sits at (80-34)/2 in the 80px row; (3) a padded display:table container lays its cell out in the content box; (4) a padded display:grid container's two 1fr tracks span the content box; (5) a unitless-zero box-shadow spread stays zero, so the shadow keeps its full 10px offset. The engine renders the same fixture through aurora-browser/tests/pageshot-probe.d --fixture at the same 1280x638 viewport (no app chrome, no scaling), and the two frames are compared pixel-for-pixel with channelTolerance 0.
